quotes.text: SharePoint was built for collaboration documents, wikis lists. Power apps was built for applications, structured relational data, transactional workflows, record level logic.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the structural mismatch behind the episode in two sentences.

quotes.text: Delegation means that the heavy lifting, the filtering, sorting, searching happens on the server close to the data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concise definition of delegation in Power Apps.

quotes.text: Once your app starts forgetting records, you're no longer dealing with a performance problem. You're dealing with a trust problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes delegation limits as a data trust issue, not just performance.

quotes.text: Governance in this context means structure, policies, roles, and automation, making sure your data isn't a digital landfill.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a practical definition of governance for list-based apps.

quotes.text: SharePoint lists are fine for prototypes, dangerous for production. They're wonderful for rapid experiments, but eventually collapse under their own pretense of simplicity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's recommendation in one memorable rule.

chapters.title: Governance and the cost of free

takeaways: Non-delegable queries against SharePoint lists silently return incomplete data once lists grow, so apps can look correct while hiding records.
SharePoint lists hit the list view threshold, throttling and item-permission overhead, while Dataverse offers relational data, role-based and field-level security and full auditing.
Use SharePoint lists for small prototypes and move apps that span departments, hold sensitive data or drive automation to Dataverse early.
hook: Clicking 'Create an app' on a SharePoint list feels like a shortcut, but it is often the mistake that later breaks your Power App. This episode is for makers and Power Platform admins who need to know when SharePoint lists are safe, why delegation and thresholds make apps lie, and when to move to Dataverse.
